memory_update.text: MOD should remain in the thermal-management liquid-cooling universe because company filings explicitly connect AI/HPC heat loads to demand for hybrid and liquid cooling.
NVT is a hidden CDU/enclosure candidate; the next filter should verify revenue materiality and AI-rack design wins rather than relying only on product existence.
INV/Accelsius is a speculative small-cap route into two-phase direct-to-chip cooling; survival depends on confirming Innventure's economic ownership and shareholder look-through exposure.
ECL/CoolIT, TT/LiquidStack and VRT/Intel validate the node as strategically important, but they are better treated as context anchors than the main underfollowed discovery lane.

Need a separate component-level pass for pumps, valves, leak detection, coolant chemistry, sensors, and third-party reliability testing; many likely suppliers are private, foreign-listed, or buried in broad industrial portfolios.

node: Thermal management and liquid-cooling component chain: CDUs, cold plates, pumps, valves, manifolds, sensors, heat exchangers, coolants, and reliability testing
summary: Layer 1B expansion found that the most direct US-listed public exposure in this node is no longer only visible in headline cooling integrators. Large-cap context anchors such as Vertiv, Trane Technologies and Ecolab validate the demand pull through acquisitions and AI-rack liquid-cooling partnerships, but the underfollowed discovery lane is more interesting in companies with narrower thermal, enclosure, CDU, heat-rejection, or two-phase cooling links. The strongest direct public candidates from this pass are Modine, nVent, and Innventure/Accelsius. SPX Technologies is included as a second-order heat-rejection and critical-HVAC candidate, but needs stricter proof that AI liquid-cooling deployments are material rather than generic data-center HVAC demand.
